findings.claim: D-419 requires a configurable WebSocket pong timeout and D-323 requires an idle timeout and a ping interval, each configurable on its own, with D-416 adding a NaruServe scheduler for ping and idle timeouts. TinyHttpd's websocket module already pings from its read loop when reads go idle for pingIntervalMillis, and it closes with 1001 after a second silent period of the same length. Its WebSocketListener has no pong callback, so NaruServe cannot see when a Pong arrives. Under D-302 (no frame codec of NaruServe's own) and D-019 (TinyHttpd is read-only), the pong timeout always equals TinyHttpd's ping interval and cannot be set separately. No item says how the three NaruServe settings map onto TinyHttpd's one setting, or that this is a TinyHttpd gap to record under D-020.
findings.evidence: /Users/beom/work/git/TinyHttpd/websocket/src/main/java/com/snoworca/tinyhttpd/websocket/WebSocket.java:271-290 (ping on idle read, close on the second timeout); /Users/beom/work/git/TinyHttpd/websocket/src/main/java/com/snoworca/tinyhttpd/websocket/WebSocketHandler.java (only pingInterval(int); 'a second silent period closes with 1001'); /Users/beom/work/git/TinyHttpd/websocket/src/main/java/com/snoworca/tinyhttpd/websocket/WebSocketListener.java (no onPong); object.md:439
findings.suggested_fix: State the mapping: TinyHttpd's pingInterval is the pong timeout (dead peer detected after 1-2x that value), the NaruServe scheduler sends application pings at the configured ping interval and enforces the idle timeout on data messages. Alternatively record the separate pong timeout as a D-020 deferred TinyHttpd gap and have wave 7 document the approximation in websocket.md and defaults.md.

findings.claim: D-417 caps the shared WebSocket sender executor at 16 threads and accepts that a stalled session holds one thread for up to 30 s. When 16 or more slow clients each have one queued message, all 16 threads are blocked for up to 30 s, and every healthy session's sends wait behind them. That breaks D-320 ('a slow client SHALL not block sends to other sessions'). A test with a single slow client still passes, so T23 would not catch it.
findings.evidence: docs/research/naruserve-v1/design/00.design.md D-417 and D-320 (section 7, 'WebSocket send queue'); /Users/beom/work/git/TinyHttpd/websocket/src/main/java/com/snoworca/tinyhttpd/websocket/WebSocket.java:206-245 (synchronous frame write under writeLock); /Users/beom/work/git/TinyHttpd/core/src/main/java/com/snoworca/tinyhttpd/TinyHttpd.java (writeTimeout default 30000)
findings.suggested_fix: Either narrow D-320 to 'fewer slow sessions than sender threads' and say so in websocket.md, or let D-417 stop dispatching to a session whose write has been in flight longer than a short threshold, closing it or applying the overflow policy. Then add a T23 case with more than 16 stalled clients next to one healthy client.

findings.claim: Shutdown is defined only for an app in NEW (D-164) and RUNNING (D-161). Nothing says what shutdown() does while listen() is still in STARTING (onStart running, or bind in progress), or in FAILED or TERMINATED. On Android, Service.onDestroy calling shutdown on a worker thread while listen() is still starting on another thread is a normal race (D-368). Two outcomes are left open: whether that listen() still reaches RUNNING, and whether onStop runs.
findings.evidence: docs/research/naruserve-v1/design/00.design.md D-161, D-164 (section 4, lifecycle); object.md:751 (first call switches atomically, repeated calls are safe)
findings.suggested_fix: Add an item: shutdown during STARTING marks a pending stop. listen() then finishes onStart, closes resources in reverse order without running onStop, leaves no socket and ends TERMINATED, and shutdown waits for that. shutdown in FAILED or TERMINATED returns with no side effects. Add a test that runs concurrent listen and shutdown.

findings.claim: TinyHttpd's WebSocketHandler.handle sends 101 and then runs the connection's whole read loop on the calling handler thread. If the TinyHttpd adapter calls it from inside the wave 4 middleware chain, D-124 means a middleware's next.run() returns only when the WebSocket connection closes. The D-173 HTTP access-log line for the upgrade request would then be written at close, not at 101 as D-325 requires. No item requires the dispatcher to finish the middleware chain before the adapter starts the handshake and read loop. Wave 4 (middleware contract) and wave 7 (TinyHttpd upgrade adapter) could each choose differently.
findings.evidence: /Users/beom/work/git/TinyHttpd/websocket/src/main/java/com/snoworca/tinyhttpd/websocket/WebSocketHandler.java:113-139 (res.upgrade then new WebSocket(...).run() on the handler thread); docs/research/naruserve-v1/design/00.design.md D-124, D-296, D-325
findings.suggested_fix: Add an item in section 3 or 7: for an upgrade request, the middleware chain and next.run() return before the 101 is sent. The adapter's upgrade extension point (D-106) performs the handshake and runs the read loop after the chain has completed. The WebSocket handler (req, ws) runs on the read thread after 101.

findings.claim: D-067 says that on the TinyHttpd adapter 'CONNECT is always answered 501 by TinyHttpd's parser'. That is wrong. TinyHttpd answers 501 only for an authority-form target. 'CONNECT /x HTTP/1.1' (origin-form) and absolute-form targets are parsed normally and reach the NaruServe handler with method CONNECT. A test built on D-067/D-400 that expects every CONNECT to bypass the access log and onError would fail.
findings.evidence: /Users/beom/work/git/TinyHttpd/core/src/main/java/com/snoworca/tinyhttpd/server/RequestParser.java:62-85 (the origin-form and absolute-form branches come before the CONNECT 501 branch)
findings.suggested_fix: Reword D-067/D-400: TinyHttpd answers 501 for CONNECT with an authority-form target. A CONNECT with an origin-form or absolute-form target reaches the router, which returns the unsupported-method result. Only the authority-form case is a TinyHttpd gap.

findings.claim: D-344 bounds shutdown at timeout plus a fixed margin, and D-107/D-223 assign that margin to the adapter release (awaitTermination). But TinyHttpd's stop(grace) itself can return up to about 1.5 s after the grace: acceptor.join(1000) plus pool.awaitWorkers(500). The force-close participants, onStop and resource closing also run after the adapter stop. A margin sized only for awaitTermination would make the T44 timing assertion flaky.
findings.suggested_fix: Make D-344's margin explicitly cover TinyHttpd's stop overrun (at least 1.5 s) plus awaitTermination. Alternatively pass grace = (time left − 1.5 s) to stop(), and record the chosen margin in lifecycle.md.

findings.claim: D-219 maps TinyHttpd's body exceptions to 413 (size), 408 (slow-body guard) and 400 (truncated or malformed). The per-read bodyReadTimeout (30 s), which D-216 keeps enabled, also throws SocketTimeoutException, and no item maps it. Under D-134 it would fall to 500. TinyHttpd itself answers 408 for any SocketTimeoutException on the body.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend D-219: any SocketTimeoutException while reading the request body (slow-body guard or bodyReadTimeout) maps to 408 with Connection: close.

findings.claim: D-154 orders the start as bind, then RUNNING, then accept. TinyHttpd.start() binds and starts the acceptor in one call, with no hook in between. So connections can be accepted, and requests parsed, before NaruServe sets RUNNING. D-156 forbids dispatching them but does not say whether the dispatcher waits for RUNNING or rejects them.
findings.evidence: /Users/beom/work/git/TinyHttpd/core/src/main/java/com/snoworca/tinyhttpd/server/HttpServer.java:128-140 ('Binds on the calling thread, then starts the acceptor and watchdog'); object.md:747
findings.suggested_fix: Add to D-156: a request that reaches the dispatcher before RUNNING waits on a start latch, and gets 503 if start fails. This keeps the order observable on adapters whose bind and accept are one call.

findings.claim: D-192 leaves the result of req.body for a JSON null body to wave 5 (kotlin.md:74 marks it (미확정)). D-194 and object.md T08 already require null to round-trip unchanged through req.body. If wave 5 chooses to throw, T08 fails, and if req.body is annotated @NonNull under D-072, the null return breaks the Kotlin contract.
findings.evidence: docs/research/naruserve-v1/design/00.design.md D-192, D-194; object.md:1040 (T08 includes null); docs/api/kotlin.md:74
findings.suggested_fix: Narrow D-192: req.body returns null for a JSON null body (as T08 requires) and is annotated @Nullable. Only the Kotlin reified extension's handling stays open.
